lee: Alert: KMS decrypt spike for service account ci-runner@prod — 120 decrypts in ~3m starting 2026-04-02T04:12:30Z. Requests from 3 distinct external IPs. tagging @anika @dave
anika: Acknowledged. I'm taking incident commander. Marta = forensics, Dave = containment/infra. Lee keep collecting evidence. I'll create an incident incident-ws and update ops doc. :rotating_light:
dave: On it. Starting containment now — will revoke ci-runner SA keys and apply egress deny for the build cluster. Posting commands I'm running:
```
# revoke token
kubectl delete secret ci-runner-token -n build || true
# apply egress deny
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-external
  namespace: build
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
EOF
```
marta: Forensics note: do NOT rotate CMK before snapshotting KMS audit logs and disk snapshots. I'm pulling KMS request logs, CloudTrail, and worker node filesystem snapshots now. Saving artifacts to s3://redwood-forensics/2026-04-02-ci-runner/
sec-bot: Alert details: rule=kms-unusual-decrypt-count severity=high src_ips=[34.120.11.45, 3.210.88.1, 52.1.9.6] user=ci-runner@prod actions=decrypt count=120 window=180s
lee: Captured the suspicious IPs and correlated with recent deploys — looks like an automated process using leaked token rather than an internal CI job. I've isolated one affected runner node: build-runner-7f9. Saving stdout logs to the incident channel.
anika: Communication plan: create short internal status update for Eng and CS. No public customer comms yet. We need: 1) scope (CI tokens), 2) impact (possible repo secrets exposed?), 3) mitigation steps, 4) next steps. @sophie can you draft?
sophie: I can draft the internal blurb. Quick Q: do we have indicators of repo pushes or artifact downloads? I'll include guidance for product teams to rotate any exposed credentials.
marta: Forensics update: I see requests with user-agent "python-requests/2.25.1" and a header set X-Forwarded-For with the src IPs. There's an itemized list in the artifact bucket. No source repo pushes found yet but scanning continues.
dave: Containment complete: ci-runner SA keys revoked at 04:17:10Z, network policy applied at 04:18:05Z, intermittent worker 172.31.9.22 quarantined (cordon + drain). Creating short-lived replacement SA for CI with least privilege and new tokens.
lee: I've rotated service-level tokens used by internal bots that referenced ci-runner creds. Also disabled legacy pipeline triggers that used that SA.
anika: Decision: rotate CMK after Marta confirms we've captured all KMS audit logs and snapshots. Marta, give go/no-go for CMK rotation.
marta: Snapshot complete at 04:22:40Z. KMS audit log export complete and integrity-checked. I give go for CMK rotation.
dave: CMK rotation scheduled and executed at 04:30:00Z. Noted in audit. Rolling keys to dependent services now.
anika: Actions assigned: - Marta: finalize forensics report and IOCs (artifact links) - Dave: ensure replacement CI SA follows least privilege and run smoke builds - Lee: compile timeline and tickets for follow-up (RBAC review, audit retention increase, adjust alerts) - Sophie: internal comms + handoff doc.
sophie: Handoff: I'm taking next 4h watch. Short summary attached in the incident doc. Key IOCs and repro steps in the artifacts.
anika: Thanks team. We'll keep the incident open for post-incident actions. Handoff to @sophie at 05:00Z. Closing immediate war-room; keep replies in this thread for any urgent new findings. :thumbsup:
lee: Added follow-up tickets: ENG-4392 (RBAC audit), SEC-2271 (increase KMS audit retention), ENG-4393 (pipeline token hygiene). I'll link them in the incident doc.
sophie: Acknowledged and will coordinate with Jira owners. I'll ping if any anomalous activity resumes.
anika: Formal incident severity: Sev2. We'll run a blameless retrospective tomorrow 10:00 PT. End of handoff.
